findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt percentage filter bypass for offer popups
findings.claim: The percentage filter previously skipped any window whose percent node was lower than the last seen value, with no log, and in app mode the offer lives inside the main Picap window whose percent can be lower, which silenced all processing (reported symptom: no logs in app mode while overlay mode worked). Offer popups identified by ID and Aceptar markers now bypass the skip; only non-popup windows (list bars) remain subject to it. Consequence: a genuinely regressed offer popup is now processed (registered, filtered, or closed) instead of ignored, which is the intended product behavior.

findings.claim: Every Picap accessibility event now emits an entry log with event type and window count plus a final no-new-order log, and every percentage decision emits a line. This adds logcat volume proportional to event rate. The instrumentation exists to pinpoint why app-mode events produced no output; once confirmed on device these lines can be downgraded or removed without affecting behavior.

findings.claim: The popup detection that protects windows from the percentage skip relies on a flattened node starting with the literal ID prefix and another containing Aceptar. If Picap changes the id format or button label, the marker check fails closed: behavior reverts to the previous skip (with the new skip log line making it visible) rather than clicking anything wrong. The risk is a silent loss of the bypass, not a misaction.
